## Verifier: **pass**

All six acceptance checks ran against the running app and passed. Built clean (`dotnet build --no-restore`: 0 warnings, 0 errors under `TreatWarningsAsErrors`). Evidence in `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/media/`.

| \# | Check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Seeded store → newest boiler reading | pass |
| 2 | Alphabetical order, not post order | pass |
| 3 | Newer reading replaces, not duplicates | pass |
| 4 | Refused sensor absent | pass |
| 5 | Empty store → `200 []` | pass |
| 6 | No route shadowing + tests pass | pass |

### What I did and saw

**Check 5 first, on a clean empty store** — started the app with the runbook's bare command (`dotnet run --project src/Readings/Readings.csproj --no-build`, ` ASPNETCORE_URLS=(127.0.0.1/redacted) no seeding).  `GET /sensors/latest`  returned  `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`  with body  `\[\]` . Not 204, not 404, not null. →  `check5-empty-store.txt\`

**Check 1** — restarted under the manifest's seeding `run` command. The three seeded boiler readings were present (18.5 / 20 / 21.5). `GET /sensors/latest` returned 200 and exactly one object: `{"sensor":"boiler","at":"2026-11-21T08:25:49+00:00","celsius":21.5,"isPlausible":true}` — the 5-minutes-ago reading. Not 18.5 (oldest), not 20.0 (the mean). → `check1-seeded-latest.txt`

**Check 2** — POSTed `cellar` **first** (202), then `attic` (202). `GET /sensors/latest` returned three objects in the order attic, boiler, cellar — alphabetical, not insertion order. → `check2-ordering.txt`

**Check 3** — POSTed boiler 22.5 at now. `/sensors/latest` still held exactly one boiler object (`grep -c` → 1), now `celsius: 22.5` at the just-posted timestamp, while `/sensors/boiler/readings` still held all four readings. Replaced, not appended. → `check3-replace-not-duplicate.txt`

**Check 4** — POSTed `shed` at -127. Got `400` with `{"error":"-127C is outside the plausible range"}`. `/sensors/latest` contained zero occurrences of `shed`, and `/sensors/shed/readings` returned `[]`. The refused reading created no key and no phantom entry. → `check4-refused-sensor.txt`

**Check 6** — `/sensors/boiler/readings` → 200, `/sensors/boiler/mean?minutes=60` → 200 with `{"mean":20.625}`. The literal route does not shadow the parameterised ones: `/sensors/latest/readings` still resolves with `sensor="latest"` (200 `[]`) and `/sensors/latest/mean?minutes=60` → 204. `POST /sensors/latest` → 405, as expected for a GET-only route. → `check6-no-route-shadowing.txt`

**Browser** — opened `/sensors/latest` in Chromium; it renders the three-element array. Only console entry is a pre-existing `favicon.ico` 404 (the app serves no static files). → `check1-2-3-4-latest-browser.png`, `console-latest.log`

### Ways I tried to make it look right but be wrong

- **POSTed an *older* attic reading (90 min ago, 5C) after the newer one.** It was accepted (202) and appears in `/sensors/attic/readings`, but `/sensors/latest` still reports attic at 30C. Taking element 0 of the newest-first list is genuinely newest, not last-written.
- **Mixed-case sensor names** (`Attic`, `Zulu`, `zulu`). Order came back `Attic, Zulu, attic, boiler, cellar, zulu` — ordinal, uppercase before lowercase, so the ordering is deterministic and not culture-dependent as the plan specified.
- **Reloaded / second GET** — identical response, no accumulation or reordering.

→ `probe-ordering-and-staleness.txt`

### Two environment notes (neither is a defect in this change)

**`dotnet test --no-build` is silent in this container.** It exits 0 but prints nothing to stdout or stderr, writes no `.trx` even with an explicit trx logger, and returns instantly. An exit code with no output cannot tell "all passed" apart from "nothing ran", so I did not accept it as evidence. Running the built assembly directly gave the real result:

```
dotnet vstest tests/Readings.Tests/bin/Debug/net9.0/Readings.Tests.dll
Passed!  - Failed: 0, Passed: 9, Skipped: 0, Total: 9
```

`--ListTests` confirms the six original facts plus the three new ones: `LatestIsTheNewestReadingPerSensor`, `LatestIsOrderedBySensorName`, `LatestOmitsASensorWithNothingStored`. The test half of check 6 passes on that evidence. → `check6-dotnet-test.txt`

**`dotnet format --verify-no-changes` exits 2 here**, with `CS0246: Fact/FactAttribute could not be found` on every `[Fact]` in the test file — including the six that predate this PR. **Pre-existing, not a regression:** a clean `git archive` of `HEAD~1` restored into a scratch directory fails identically. It is an SDK/workspace resolution quirk (container resolves SDK 11.0.100; no `global.json`), not a code problem — the build itself resolves xunit fine at 0 warnings. It is also not an acceptance check, and the manifest deliberately drops it from the sandbox.

Both are written up in `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/sandbox-report.json` so the test command can be made self-evidencing.

### Housekeeping

App stopped, browser closed, no process left on 5080, scratch checkout removed. The only working-tree change is the `.gitignore` edit that was already present when I started.

*Note: `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/app.json` did not exist, so I started the app myself per the manifest's `run` command rather than attaching to a pre-running sandbox.*
